chunks: And from him, from Ibn Bint Ilyas, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
"Indeed, Hajj and Umrah remove poverty and sins, just as the bellows removes impurities from iron."

key_terms.الْكِير: Bellows (used in blacksmithing to blow air on fire)

ai.seo_question: How do Hajj and Umrah remove sins and poverty according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the dual benefit of Hajj and Umrah is highlighted as both spiritual purification and material alleviation. The metaphor of the bellows (*kir*) refining iron illustrates how these pilgrimages burn away the dross of sins and poverty, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the transformative power of divine grace through ritual devotion.
